text.p: Hong Kong stocks opened sharply higher on Wednesday, with the blue-chip Hang Seng Index storming to an all-time high of 15,895, up 123 points or 0.78 percent, in the first few minutes of trade.
"Blue chips are generally higher this morning on the strength of Cheung Kong and Hutchison," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
Cheung Kong was up HK$2.00 to HK$80.00 due to the good reponse to the developer's recent sale of flats, brokers said.
Hutchison touched a record high of HK$75.50 in early trade before retreating to trade HK$0.25 lower at HK$74.50.
The stock has risen more than seven percent this week on Hutchison's new agreements in China's telecoms sector.
"Following the market's recent uptrend and higher U.S. stock and bond prices, the Hang Seng should continue its record-breaking rally," said Percy Au-Young, research director at DBS Securities.
He said the index was likely to test 16,000 later on Wednesday as September index futures had risen to 16,020.
Index futures related trading could affect the movement of the Hang Seng ahead of the expiry of July contracts in the afternoon, brokers said.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index for red chips added 29 points, or 0.86 percent, to 3,494.
Shanghai Industrial was up HK$1.00 to HK$53.75 and Founder added HK$0.25 to HK$6.60, but COSCO Pacific eased HK$0.15 to HK$17.00.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index was down seven points, or 0.65 percent, to 1,142.
Guangdong Kelon lost HK$0.85 to HK$9.90 after the company said it agreed to place 76.598 million new H-shares at HK$9.20 each to private investors.
